transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this case conference as part of our standard pre-filing practice before I make the decision on whether to authorize the preliminary-injunction filing. As you all know, a former sales executive departed last week and joined a direct competitor, and we have reason to believe confidential customer information may have been used after the departure. We potentially have a three-week window to request a preliminary-injunction hearing. The draft filing currently seeks broad relief covering customer information, pricing materials, and source-code documentation. Before I sign off on authorization, I need each of you to report any material issues in your respective areas. Let's start with employment counsel, then forensics, then insurance. Are there any material concerns or prerequisites any of you need to flag before we proceed?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a material issue. While reviewing the former executive's archived personnel file, I found a signed separation agreement that contains an exclusive forum clause. This clause requires any disputes concerning confidential information to be filed in Illinois state court in Cook County, where the executive worked. I have not yet added this clause to the draft strategy memorandum, but it could significantly affect where we file and potentially the scope of relief we can seek. We need to consider this before authorizing the filing.
